claims.claim: Grown models generalize better than fixed-size models trained from scratch.

findings.claim: Grown models converge to flatter minima than fixed-size models trained from scratch.
findings.rationale: Flatter minima are associated with better generalization; this finding supports the hypothesis that growing networks improve optimization landscape.
findings.recommendation: Further empirical validation across architectures and datasets is recommended.

findings.claim: Grown models generalize better than fixed-size models trained from scratch.
findings.rationale: Improved generalization is a key outcome of flatter minima, suggesting practical benefits of the growing approach.
findings.recommendation: Investigate whether the generalization gain holds under different training schedules.

open_questions: Does the flatter minima effect persist when growing networks are applied to very deep architectures?
What is the computational overhead of the growing procedure compared to training fixed-size models?
summary: The paper shows that incrementally growing neural networks during training leads to flatter minima and better generalization compared to fixed-size models trained from scratch.
